blocks.html: True also that, on the other hand, it does not seem very hard to answer the reasons deduced by the accused. For as to saying, first, that more faith must be given to the witnesses who depose for the prisoner, because they affirm: this reason cannot be fitted to this case, for the other witnesses also, or the greater part, assure — namely, that the accused is Arnauld du Tilh. Added to which, the negation they make, that the prisoner is not Martin Guerre, comes easily into proof, inasmuch as they restrict themselves so well to places, times and persons that we are outside the terms of that common rule, that two witnesses who affirm are more credible than a thousand who deny.
